reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, the geometry of the partition is associated with several measured factors. Tissue source site shows the strongest location association with candidate-generation consensus geometry (PERMANOVA R^2 0.254, q=0.0025) with no dispersion difference (PERMDISP p=0.395). CT phase (R^2 0.154) and CT manufacturer (R^2 0.059) show significant PERMANOVA but also significant PERMDISP, so their geometry effects may reflect both location and dispersion and cannot be cleanly attributed to location alone. Continuous CT acquisition factors show significant distance-regression associations (slice thickness R^2 0.136, z-spacing R^2 0.142, both q=0.002; pixel spacing R^2 0.019 and study year R^2 0.029, small but significant). CT scanner model and reconstruction kernel are not significant after correction. These partition-wide geometry associations indicate that measured technical, acquisition, and site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for partition geometry; they do not establish technical artifact or causation, and R^2 values are univariable and must not be summed.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This geometry-level confounder evidence is consistent with the partition-scope categorical associations and with the prior cross-modal reports: the same factors (site, CT phase, manufacturer, slice/z spacing) that are non-randomly distributed across the partition also show geometry associations.
